subject: BrightLayer security questionnaire — data residency & retention (hosted API)
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@brightlayer.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightLayer Security <security@brightlayer.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: BrightLayer security questionnaire — hosted API data residency/retention

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightLayer is excited about the Redwood platform. Our security team is working through the standard vendor questionnaire and had a couple specific questions on hosted API behavior for data residency, retention, and deletion. I’ve attached the latest SQ (BrightLayer_SQ_v2.xlsx) and pulled out the three items we want to confirm quickly: 

1) Where is customer data (request/response payloads, logs, embeddings) stored for Redwood Hosted API? Can you provide region-level options and whether we can restrict storage to a single region?

2) What are your default retention windows for request/response logs and derived artifacts (embeddings, cache metadata)? Is there a way to shorten these for regulated accounts?

3) Describe the deletion/erasures process for hosted tenants. Do you provide an API or portal to request a tenant-level purge, and what is the expected timeline (including backups and snapshots)?

We’re on a tight procurement timeline — a short, explicit response to each item would be ideal. Happy to hop on a call if that’s faster.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Security Operations
BrightLayer
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightLayer security questionnaire — hosted API data residency/retention

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list and the attachment. Below are concise answers to the three items; I’ve also attached a one‑page summary (Redwood_BrightLayer_SQ_Response.pdf) and flagged the bits that require contract (DPA/SLA) language.

1) Region & storage: 
- Customer request/response payloads are stored in a customer‑scoped data plane located in the cloud region you choose at onboarding (we support us-west-2, us-east-1, and eu-west-1 for Hosted accounts today).
- You can restrict processing and persistent storage to a single region; we enforce routing policies that pin all active inference and storage to that region for the tenant.
- Metadata about routing decisions and non-persistent telemetry (aggregated infra metrics) may be replicated for operational health across regions, but these do not contain customer prompt/response text.

2) Default retention windows: 
- Request/response logs (text payloads): default 90 days for hosted eval/troubleshooting logs.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, vector cache): default 365 days. Embeddings are considered customer data and stored in the tenant data plane.
- Shortening retention: enterprise accounts can opt into custom retention policies at onboarding via the Console or as part of the DPA; we can reduce text log retention to as low as 0 days (ephemeral) and embeddings to 30 days, subject to feature constraints (e.g., long-term reranking requires longer retention).

3) Deletion / erasure process: 
- Tenant-level purge: we offer a documented tenant erasure operation via support request and Customer Console (Self-Serve for Dedicated/Private; support-assisted for Hosted).
- Timeline: primary data plane deletion completes within 72 hours of an approved purge request. Full scrubbing from backups/snapshots is on a 30‑ to 90‑day schedule depending on when snapshot windows fall; we provide a certificate of deletion after the 90‑day backlog window if required by audits.
- API: we provide an API for programmatic erasures for customers with enterprise contracts. For standard Hosted accounts, we use a support workflow with SLA-backed timelines.

If useful, Neha can add the precise DPA clause language for retention/backup timing. Rishi is looping in on TLS/KMS items referenced in your worksheet. Happy to set a quick call to walk through the attached answers.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Strategic Accounts (Redwood Inference)
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@brightlayer.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightLayer Security <security@brightlayer.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightLayer security questionnaire — hosted API data residency/retention

Jonas — this is very helpful, thanks. Two quick clarifications from our side: 

• For the 72‑hour primary deletion window, does that include derived artifacts (embeddings) stored in the tenant vector store, or is that only for raw request/response logs?

• Regarding backups/snapshots, can you confirm whether backups are region‑scoped (i.e., backups stored only in the customer region) or if they are replicated to a secondary region for disaster recovery? We need explicit confirmation on whether backups of customer data ever leave the region.

If you can confirm both points in a short reply we can close this section of the SQ.

—Aisha
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, BrightLayer Security <security@brightlayer.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Nov 2028 13:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightLayer security questionnaire — hosted API data residency/retention

Hi Aisha — quick clarifications: 

• 72‑hour purge window covers primary storage layers including request/response logs and tenant vector store contents. Embeddings are deleted from the live tenant store within 72 hours; however, if an embedding exists in an archived snapshot it will follow the backup retention scrub window (30–90 days), as mentioned earlier. We can add an optional policy to accelerate snapshot retention for enterprise customers (contract amendment).

• Backups & replication: for Hosted accounts configured as single‑region, backups/snapshots are region‑scoped by default. We do offer an explicit cross‑region replication option for DR that is off by default and requires opt‑in via a signed configuration agreement; when enabled, replication targets are listed in the Console and documented in the DPA.

Next steps: I’ve attached the PDF summary and updated the spreadsheet with the answers inline. If BrightLayer wants the snapshot purge acceleration we can surface that as a commercial addendum in the SOW.

I’m available Mon and Tue for a short call if you’d like to finalize wording for procurement.

Best,
Jonas
